classification.difficultyReason: Students generalise from the horizontal cases and transfer the comparison to vertical output operations. The circle format limits the response, but the vertical clause supplies no pair of operations to test.

content.prompt: In general, when applying two types of horizontal transformations, order matters/does not matter (circle one). When applying two types of vertical transformations, order matters/does not matter (circle one).

answer.short: Horizontal transformations: order matters. Vertical transformations: order matters.
answer.worked: For horizontal transformations, a right translation by $1$ followed by replacing $x$ with $2x$ gives $f(2x-1)$. Reversing the order gives $f(2x-2)$. For vertical transformations, an upward translation by $1$ followed by doubling the outputs gives $2(f(x)+1)$. Reversing the order gives $2f(x)+1$. Order can affect the result in both cases.
